basic_identification.full_title: Treatment and Disposal of Steel Plant Effluents — Guidelines (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Environment and Ecology / Water Pollution Control (approved by the newly established Environment and Ecology Division Council and finalized by the Water Pollution Control Sectional Committee, EED 03, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies guidelines, technical criteria, and treatment methods for managing, segregating, treating, and safely disposing of various effluent and wastewater streams generated during steel plant operations (including coke ovens, blast furnaces, steelmaking furnaces, rolling mills, and pickling lines) to enable in-plant recycling and prevent environmental pollution.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Guidelines / Code of Practice (Environmental Protection / Water Pollution Control)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Procedural and Guidelines Standard. Although IS 8073:2026 is an engineering code of practice and operational guideline rather than a direct consumer product carrying an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp, its structural requirements, segregation strategies, chemical neutralizing schemes, and biological treatments are legally enforced across India by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs). Compliance is mandatory to secure and maintain a steel plant's statutory Consent to Operate (CTO) and Consent to Establish (CTE). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Because treating all waste streams to a quality suitable for in-plant recirculation is economically unviable, plants must strictly segregate cooling water streams and less contaminated wastes from highly contaminated process wastes.

In all treatment cases, the potential for effluents to cause chemical corrosion of steel plant metals and concrete structures must be eliminated through active treatments, including super-phosphate (phosphatization) and lime (alkalization).

Wastewater from blast furnace gas cleaning and cooling must be treated by plain sedimentation in horizontal-flow sedimentation tanks (without coagulants) to reduce suspended solids (SS) to standard limits (e.g., 10 mg/l).

Spent pickle liquor from acid pickling lines must be chemically regenerated or neutralized with lime. Adding lime and air under controlled temperature and aeration conditions oxidizes ferrous hydroxide into rapidly settling and insoluble ferric hydroxide. Acid and copperas (ferrous sulphate heptahydrate) must be recovered from pickle liquor to the maximum extent economically possible.
Acid sludge generated from by-product plants is classified as hazardous waste and must be safely disposed of in a Secured Land Fill (SLF).
Caustic wash waste generated from by-product plants must be disposed of via incineration.
Brine wastewater from ion exchange resin regeneration must either be chemically reclaimed or discharged via highly controlled release to wastewater streams.
Spent cleaners utilized in surface treatment and degreasing must be segregated for oil breakout or incineration.

Coke oven wastes are rich in nitrogen but relatively low in phosphorus. Because phosphorus is required to the extent of approximately 1 percent of the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) for microbial growth, phosphorus must be supplemented during biological coke oven waste treatment.

Phenolic substances in coke oven waste demand high levels of dissolved oxygen (2 mg to 25 mg of oxygen per milligram of phenol). Biological systems must maintain adequate oxygen supplies, and plants must provide dedicated handling facilities for the substantial quantities of excess sludge generated.

requirements.requirement_type: Scale Pit Dredging and Turbulence Control
requirements.detail: Settled scale from rolling mill wastewater must be dredged from scale pits using buckets or drag-out conveyors. To prevent scale from passing over the weir, turbulent conditions must be minimized by shutting down the specific compartment of the scale pit being cleaned.

Slurry containing fly ash from power plants must be pumped to settling basins or low-lying dyked areas. The supernatant water can be reused or discharged, but the raw slurry must never be discharged directly into streams or freshwater lakes.

Ammonia and phenols must be recovered from coke oven waste to the maximum extent economically possible. The remaining wastewater can be treated in an extended aeration activated sludge process working on a complete mixing system.
If raw sewage or dilution water is available, coke oven waste can be diluted to a phenol concentration below 200 mg/l and treated in a trickling filter.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 8073 : 2026 (First Revision) is the mandatory national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for the treatment, recirculation, and disposal of effluents originating from integrated iron and steel plants. Formulated by the Water Pollution Control Sectional Committee (EED 03), this standard regulates the segregation of highly contaminated process streams from cooling waters to facilitate cost-effective in-plant recycling. It establishes strict handling and treatment rules for hazardous coke oven, pickling, and gas-cleaning wastes—mandating the chemical neutralization and regeneration of spent pickling acids, the recovery of ammonia and phenols, phosphorus nutrient supplementation for biological aeration, and safe land or incineration disposal for hazardous sludges and caustic washes to satisfy national pollution control limits.
